newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fundamentals, sentiment boost Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Fundamentals, sentiment boost Brussels bourse.

text.p: Signs of accelerating economic growth, low interest rates and fading fears of new turmoil around the European Union's single currency project combined to lift the Brussels bourse to record highs on Monday.
"All this news is going to sustain the market this week, but levels are now so high that we are seeing very few institutional buyers," a trader said. "The volumes are quite low".
The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares .BFX was up 22.80 points, or 0.99 percent, at 2,332.73 at 0900 GMT, having earlier set an intra-day high of 2,336.55.
Among the main gainers was Kredietbank, up 3.9 percent to 15,875 francs, on continued speculation of a strategic alliance with another bank or banks, traders said.

Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere, which climbed more than 12 percent last week as the company found renewed favour with foreign investors due to the strong dollar and rising zinc prices, was again a strong performer.
The stock was up 2.3 percent to 3,275 francs, and was again one of the busier issues on the bourse.
Retailer Colruyt, steel cord and wire maker Bekaert and banker Dexia also gained.
Traders said the strong and stable dollar was the main force behind the strength of these shares.
On the downside, fast food chain Quick and oil major PetroFina were bucking the positive trend. Traders said they were at a loss to explain why.
Quick was down 1.0 percent at 1,980 francs, while PetroFina was down 0.2 percent at 12,450 francs.
